trust_decision.summary: Reject, inside the codec: psd_tools.compression.decompress must raise instead of black-filling a failed channel when the would-be output (width*height*depth/8) is both over 16 MiB and over 1000x the compressed input; in parallel, check_pixel_size gains a channel term and an opt-in module-level byte budget (MAX_ALLOC_BYTES, default None) applied at the numpy and PIL composite entry points.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'composite/numpy ... crafted PSD geometry', so the first thing read is the numpy render path, whose only guard is the pre-existing check_pixel_size(width, height) at src/psd_tools/api/utils.py:41 - a per-axis 30,000 px limit that 5964x10296 passes.

fix_sites.entry_point: psd_tools.compression.decompress() (public, docs/reference/psd_tools.compression.rst:13); reached from ImageData.get_data, ChannelData.get_data and Pattern.get_data
api.utils.check_pixel_size(), shared helper called by PSDImage.numpy(), PSDImage.topil() and psd_tools.composite.composite()

O3_reason_to_dismiss: psd_tools.compression is a documented general-purpose codec whose stated contract is to always return bytes and degrade a failed channel to black with a PSDDecompressionWarning (src/psd_tools/compression/__init__.py:89-101, pinned tests tests/psd_tools/compression/test_compression.py:165-195), so a solver can argue that raising there is the caller's job and that the codec path is out of scope for 'composite/numpy'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A failed decode below the data-aware threshold must still be replaced by black pixels with a PSDDecompressionWarning rather than raising, and a within-spec canvas must not be rejected (the byte budget is opt-in, MAX_ALLOC_BYTES defaults to None).

O6_input_shapes: compression method: RAW / RLE / ZIP / ZIP_WITH_PREDICTION failure paths all converge on one fallback
bit depth 8 / 16 / 32 (the black fill is built as PIL mode L / RGBA)
channel count 1..56 (header validator) and the merged-image height*channels passed as the codec's height
entry surfaces: merged ImageData, layer ChannelData, pattern channel data, and a direct decompress() call
numpy shortcut channel='mask'/'shape' allocating np.ones without touching any channel data

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PSDImage.composite() / Layer.composite() / Group.composite() reach psd_tools.composite.composite(), which calls check_pixel_size on the viewport only and then allocates the Compositor viewport buffers (colour, alpha, shape) at 4 bytes/px/channel before any channel is decoded, so the byte budget introduced by the fix never applies there.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: MAX_ALLOC_BYTES is opt-in and was added for the numpy/PIL render paths; composite() is a separate path that needs optional aggdraw/scipy/scikit-image, and its 30,000 px per-axis guard is argued to be sufficient.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one file in the composite/ package, two call hops from the landing point (psd_image.py:338 -> composite/composite.py:188)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The Compositor constructor allocates the viewport buffers from the declared viewport geometry alone (np.zeros/np.full of (height, width, 1..channels)), which is the same declared-geometry-to-allocation shape the advisory is about and is reached before the layer channel data is read.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The buffers are float32 working state of a documented compositor whose size is bounded by the per-axis 30,000 px limit, so a solver can call it a design limit rather than part of the compression guard.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same module as the composite() route, one function below

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second merged-image call site that multiplies height by channels (or by depth//8) before handing geometry to the codec - e.g. a PSB or 16/32-bit variant of get_data().
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The length the allocator uses is computed at this call site rather than inside the codec, so a maintainer hardening 'declared geometry to allocation' would naturally add a sibling check here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A viewport-size guard in Compositor.__init__ before the colour/alpha/shape buffers are allocated.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The compositor is the one place that knows both the viewport and the channel count it is about to allocate, so a maintainer could plausibly have guarded it there instead of in check_pixel_size.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A declared-size check in _create_image before Image.frombytes allocates the declared (width, height).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same declared-geometry-to-allocation shape as the Image.new at src/psd_tools/compression/__init__.py:231, one layer higher in the PIL adapter.

O9_family: uncontrolled memory allocation from attacker-declared PSD geometry (CWE-789, memory-exhaustion DoS)
